title: General switching lemma for DNFs
statement:
Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n \ge 1$ Boolean variables whose width is at most $w$, where $w \ge 1$, and let $p \in \bbr$ satisfy $0 < p \le 1$ together with $p \le \tfrac{1}{40w}$. Draw a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction $\rho$, which independently leaves each of the $n$ variables free with probability $p$ and otherwise fixes it to a uniformly random Boolean value, and let $f_\rho$ denote the function of the free variables obtained by evaluating $f$ with the fixed coordinates set according to $\rho$. Then for every $t \in \bbn$,
\[
  \bbP_\rho\!\left[\operatorname{depth}(f_\rho) > t\right]
  \;\le\; \left(\tfrac12\right)^{t} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{np}{3}\right),
\]
where $\operatorname{depth}(f_\rho)$ is the decision-tree depth of $f_\rho$, i.e.\ the least depth of a decision tree computing it.
hypotheses_covered: f is a DNF formula on n variables
width of f is at most w
t is an arbitrary natural number
replaced:
Let $f$ be a DNF of width at most $w$ with $0<w$ and $0<n$, and let $p\in\bbr$ satisfy
$0<p$, $p\le \tfrac{1}{40w}$ and $p\le 1$. Then for every $t\in\bbn$,
\[
\mathrm{bernoulliRestrProb}\,p\,\bigl(\rho \mapsto \mathrm{dtDepth}(\mathrm{restrictFn}\,f.\mathrm{eval}\,\rho) > t\bigr)
\;\le\; \bigl(\tfrac12\bigr)^{t} + \exp\!\bigl(-np/3\bigr).
\]
Unlike the base version, no syntactic non-duplication hypothesis is required, since the
formula is first cleaned.
